newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel diffs up sharply late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel diffs up sharply late.

text.p: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel differentials skysrocketed higher late Wednesday with few barrels available for prompt trade.
NYMEX heating oil prices, however, shed 1.01 cents by the close in a very volatile technical trading session. Gasoline futures slipped 1.07 cents by the settlement.

U.S. Gulf (USG) low sulphur diesel for delivery on the back 4th cycle of the Colonial Pipeline changed hands as high as 5.00 cents over the screen near the NYMEX close, traders said, up about 2.0 cents from Tuesday. However, late day offers pulled back to about 4.0 cents over.
Much of that buying interest was due to traders covering short positions, according to market watchers.
New York Harbor (NYH) prompt low sulphur diesel barrels were offered at 3.80 cents over the screen, up from about 3.00 cents over yesterday, though activity there was fairly thin.
"There's no real low sulphur barrels around on offer, so the market's tight," one trader said.
NYH No. 2 oil diffs also firmed, according to players, with prompt barrels offered at 3.00 cents above the NYMEX, up nearly 1.00 cent on the day.
USG No. 2 oil for back 4th cycle delivery changed hands at 0.75 cents over the print, about 0.5 cent stronger.
